summary.name: Pixilation (supplemental design reference, not a directly named style in the source collection)
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: live performers are animated through deliberately photographed poses that keep scene and costume continuity. Sliding, unexpected position changes, and object interaction are planned with readable direction and exposure holds. It is distinct from pixel art and from simply lowering a continuous video's frame rate.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: the source says to use Pixilation alone for surreal performance. Inferred: hybrids suit music-driven or annotated pieces, such as music videos and energetic social campaigns. Product, editorial, or explanatory uses are unspecified for this style itself.
summary.limitations: Explicit: it requires photographed live performers posed frame by frame, and low-frame-rate footage is not an acceptable substitute. Avoid beat flashing, continuity breaks, faking with low-fps footage, and covering faces. No visual renderer is listed for this style.
summary.palette: Explicit, optional example only: background #EEE7DC, foreground #343C43, accent #8A9288, applied to new presentation elements. Foreground on background is 9.127 contrast and passes normal text. Accent on foreground is 3.495, so it is decorative only. Task or brand colors override these; photographs, costumes, and materials stay unchanged, and gradients are disabled.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: motion is stepped exposure with pose jumps and held states. Preserve planned exposure rate and holds, and do not automatically generate in-between poses. Delivery frame rate may exceed exposure rate. Interaction is unspecified for this style; any interactive delivery must remain optional and not required for video export.
summary.audio: Unspecified: the source gives no fixed soundtrack or voice requirement. Inferred: music can sync to pose jumps at section changes, while sound effects or silence can clarify key actions and reading holds. Speech must stay intelligible. Use only user-chosen or authorized audio, and do not invent audio assets.
summary.assetRequirements: Explicit: prepared performer frames should have consistent dimensions, clear naming, and transparency where layered. Numbered frame sequences and a layer manifest are listed as inputs, and assets must be inspected before composition. Fonts and assets should load before rendering. Frame counts, duration, and aspect ratio are unspecified and treated as optional examples.
summary.combinations: Explicit: Pixilation is recommended alone for surreal performance. Suggested hybrid one pairs it with style-105 so beat-aligned exposure holds and position jumps follow a verified beat table. Suggested hybrid two pairs it with style-093 for kinetic type stepping on the photo cadence. Both referenced styles are undefined in this source.
summary.productionApproach: Explicit: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition, timing, audio sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. Visual and motion layers own the poses and movement. FFmpeg encodes sequences, Python preprocesses assets, and chroma.js checks colors. Inspect decoded opening, action, transition, and closing frames before delivery.
